pr.title: fix(stack): submit/merge now understand non-trunk stack parents better
pr.body:
<!-- git-stk:description -->
A stack rooted on a branch other than the trunk - a release line, say - keeps that parentless root in its line. That root is the base the branch above it targets, not a layer of the stack: `restack` and `absorb` already skip it, but `submit` demanded a parent for every branch in scope, and `merge` treated it as the stack bottom.

`stack::stacked_layers` states the rule once, and `submit` and `merge` now follow it.

- **submit:** stack mode ships what `--no-stack` always did, and leaves the base out of the `-u --force-with-lease` push and the review-body steps. It was refusing a shape `new` and `adopt` both create.
- **merge:** never lands the base review. A release branch with an open PR into the trunk became the stack bottom, and the base check that would have caught it is skipped for a branch with no recorded parent. `merge --all` counted it among the reviews to land, too.
- **errors:** "no stack parent" now names the branch being acted on and points at `git stk adopt --parent <base>` rather than a bare `git stk adopt`, which silently adopts onto the trunk - destructive when the branch is a release line.

`sync` reaches the same bad metadata from another direction; filed as #308, where the narrow fixes conflict with its metadata-rebuild job.
<!-- /git-stk:description -->

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #307
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: merge --all pins the stack base as the first branch of the line, but sync still records the base's own review as its stack parent, so the base can be adopted, restacked onto the trunk, merged, or deleted as finished.

prior_bot.note: bot traced sync re-recording the base's parent and landing it; the PR answered with the pinned_base workaround that 310 replaced
